about.title: Jurupa Valley Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Jurupa Valley residents encounter defective products in ordinary settings — a faulty vehicle part while driving near SR-60 or Limonite Avenue, a malfunctioning tool at a warehouse job, or a household appliance that fails without warning. California follows a strict liability framework for these cases, meaning the person hurt generally doesn't need to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product itself was defective in design, manufacturing, or warnings, and that the defect caused harm. That standard can apply to the maker, the distributor, or the retailer that sold it. If you were injured by something that broke, malfunctioned, or lacked adequate safety instructions, keeping the item itself — not just photos of it — can matter for building a claim. We evaluate the product, the injury, and the timeline at no upfront cost.

items.desc: Because California allows strict liability claims, you may not need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which widens the paths we can explore on your behalf.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving the Product
items.desc: We can advise you early on keeping the defective item intact, since the product itself often serves as central evidence in these claims.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability approach, you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, rather than proving the company acted carelessly. We can review your situation and explain how this standard applies to your specific case.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, including any packaging, parts, or instructions. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, since it may be needed as evidence. Our team can advise on safe storage.

items.question: I was hurt by a product while driving near Limonite Avenue or SR-60 in Jurupa Valley — does that change anything?
items.answer: Location itself doesn't change the legal standard, but details like where and when the incident occurred can help establish the timeline of your claim. Jurupa Valley sees regular collision activity along corridors like SR-60 and Limonite Avenue, so documenting exactly what happened, including any vehicle part failure, is still useful. We can help sort out whether the claim involves a defective product, another driver, or both.

items.question: Do you charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No, contacting us for a free case review costs nothing. We typically work on contingency, meaning we're only paid if you recover compensation.
